means: A two-person framing: we stand behind one character's shoulder and look past it at the other, so a near shoulder and the back of a head sit blurred in the foreground.
does: It can land - the shot_framing_type over_shoulder panel has a genuine blurred foreground head at frame left with the subject facing us across it. But read the clause that produced it: "over the shoulder, 2boys, blurry foreground shoulder". The literal foreground noun is doing at least as much work as the OTS tag. THIS IS DANBOORU GRAMMAR: it requires a character count of two, and count tags (1boy / 2boys / solo / no humans) are resolved FIRST and bend everything else around them. Put "over the shoulder" in a prompt that also says "1boy, solo" and it loses - the project's card review found six of ten framing options collapsing back to the same lone figure for exactly this reason.
reach_for_it: dialogue coverage between two characters - and only after you have changed the count tag to 2boys or 2girls and removed solo. Spell out the foreground: "blurry foreground shoulder" or "from behind".
used_in: shot.framing_type over_shoulder. FILM-CRAFT-AUDIT.md separately lists "over the shoulder" and "reverse angle" as unreliable tokens for the video pass - write direction as geometry there instead.
